D1.title: Effort estimate per solution option
D1.purpose: Every requirement of the client's list estimated per solution option: the approach (greenfield: standard, partial, custom; migration: keep, adapt, convert to standard, rebuild, retire, new), a {estimation.size_term.en} size with its derivation and basis, the effort from the editable size mapping, on top the PM, SA, BA and QA surcharges and the fixed phases per option - every total and every cost as a formula.
D1.sources_client: The client's requirement list as received; per requirement and option an estimate against the vendor's documentation and standard code and - for a migration - the code analysis of today's shop; the consolidated phases, exclusions and risks; verified technology facts.
D1.extra: Sizes are {estimation.size_term.en} sizes; the effort in {estimation.unit} follows from the mapping on the Parameters sheet, as do the surcharges per option and the day rate. Change a value there and every total, cost and chart follows. No total is typed; only the fixed phases carry an entered, editable effort.

sheets.name: Parameters
sheets.readme: day rate, sprint limit, {estimation.size_term.en} mapping and surcharges per option - editable; every total, cost and chart recomputes

rows.name: Day rate
rows.meaning: day rate in {estimation.currency} for the cost per option - an order of magnitude, not an offer

rows.name: Sprint limit
rows.meaning: from this effort in {estimation.unit} a requirement does not fit a sprint ({last:estimation.sizes}, flagged); anything larger is split into positions

rows.name: Scenario
rows.meaning: the scenario the single-scenario sheets show (client lists, Estimation, Totals, key figures); chosen from the table of scenarios

sheets.name: {p.name}
sheets.readme: The client's list as received (list “{p.sheet}”, columns unchanged and in their order), beside it per system the effort in the selected scenario (sheet Parameters): the sum of the work packages that roll up to the row, of which conditional and of which interim solution, the number of work packages and the impact per system

sheets.name: Other_Rows
sheets.readme: Rows that are on no list of the client (technical rows without a client row, interfaces, added sections) - per system their effort in the selected scenario; together with the client lists they make up the whole development (reconciliation on sheet Totals)

sheets.name: Requirements
sheets.readme: The client's requirement list as received - the reference for every trace

sheets.name: Estimation
sheets.readme: One row per work package (requirement × system × option, for a dependent system per base option), grouped by requirement: starting point, coverage, approach, {estimation.size_term.en} size, effort from the {estimation.size_term.en} mapping (with positions their sum) with its range by the certainty of the estimate (sheet Parameters), estimation assumptions and basis; rows of other owners are empty input cells

sheets.name: Estimation
sheets.readme: One row per requirement, one column block per option: approach, {estimation.size_term.en} size, effort from the {estimation.size_term.en} mapping (the sum of its positions where it has some), note on the sprint limit, estimation assumptions and basis; collapsed: evidence, derivation, mechanism

set.readme: One row per requirement (client requirement, technical migration, refactoring), one column block per option: approach, {estimation.size_term.en} size, effort from the {estimation.size_term.en} mapping (for positions their sum), sprint-limit note, effort on {estimation.integration_platform}, estimation assumptions and basis; for refactoring the saving in the migration

sheets.name: Estimation_Positions
sheets.readme: Requirements above the sprint limit, split into positions (each at most {last:estimation.sizes}); their effort on the Estimation sheet is the sum of these rows

sheets.name: Estimation_Positions
sheets.readme: Work packages above the sprint limit, cut into positions (each at most {last:estimation.sizes}); their effort on sheet Estimation is the sum of these rows

sheets.name: Surcharges_and_Phases
sheets.readme: Per option: the development (sum of the estimation), the PM, SA, BA and QA surcharges (rates from the Parameter sheet) and the fixed phases incl. the technical migration tasks without a requirement - their effort is editable

set.readme: Per scenario: the {target.platform} development of its row classes (sum of the estimate), the saving through refactoring, the surcharges PM, SA, BA and QA (rates from the Parameters sheet), the scenario's fixed phases - their effort is editable - and the {estimation.integration_platform} development with the same surcharges

sheets.name: Surcharges_and_Phases
sheets.readme: Per system and option: the development (sum of the work packages on sheet Estimation; a dependent system per base option), the surcharges PM, SA, BA and QA (rates from sheet Parameters, on inputs of other owners only on request) and the fixed phases - their effort is editable

set.purpose: Every requirement of the client's list and every technical migration and refactoring row estimated per solution option: the approach, a {estimation.size_term.en} size with derivation and basis, the effort from the editable size mapping - for {target.platform} and {estimation.integration_platform} separately -, on top the PM, SA, BA and QA surcharges and the fixed phases per scenario; every total and cost is a formula.

set.title: Effort estimate per system
set.purpose: Every requirement that touches a system of this solution estimated as a work package per system and option: starting point, coverage, approach, a {estimation.size_term.en} size with derivation and basis, the effort from the editable size mapping with its range; systems of other owners as empty input cells; per system and option the surcharges and fixed phases; the client's lists with the effort per system beside them - every total and cost a formula.
set.sources_client: The client's lists as received; the impact of every row per system; per work package an estimate against the vendor's documentation; the decisions on gaps; the consolidated phases, exclusions and risks; verified technology facts.
set.extra: Sizes are {estimation.size_term.en} sizes; the effort in {estimation.unit_short.en} follows from the mapping on sheet Parameters, as do the range, the surcharges per system and option, the day rate and the scenario shown. Change a value there and every total, all costs and every chart follow. Inputs of other owners (empty, shaded cells on sheet Estimation) count in every total as soon as they are entered.

readme.basis_handover: “Code analysis · <id>” – a row of the released code analysis of today's shop (the requirement, task or unit it describes); the places in the code are listed there, not in this workbook

set.glossary_text: Standard = documented capability of the vendor product in the stated version. Custom = built or to be built for {engagement.client}. Code analysis = the released analysis of today's shop; the basis names the row an estimate rests on (requirement, task or unit).

Standard = documented capability of the vendor product in the named version. Work package = one requirement in one system and option. Gap = not solvable in that system; where the work goes is on sheet Completeness. Scenario = one option per system.
